title: Footnotes Gone Feral
blurb: The parts of history your textbook skipped because nobody would believe them.

cards.say: [Olympic medals were once handed out for painting and poetry], [tug of war was an official Olympic sport for 20 years], [a runner in the 1904 Olympic marathon rode part of the way in a car], and [Olympic gold medals were made of solid gold until 1948].
cards.real: The last solid gold Olympic medals were awarded in 1912. Gold medals since then are mostly silver with a gold coating.

cards.say: [Abraham Lincoln is in the National Wrestling Hall of Fame], [Thomas Jefferson was the first president to live in the White House], [Martin Van Buren grew up speaking Dutch, not English], and [President Taft kept a cow named Pauline on the White House lawn].
cards.real: John Adams moved into the unfinished White House in November 1800, a few months before Jefferson took office.

cards.say: [The Pony Express carried mail across the West for twelve years], [in 1914 a little girl in Idaho was mailed to her grandparents], [the US Navy and Post Office once delivered mail by cruise missile], and [the Hope Diamond was sent to the Smithsonian by ordinary mail].
cards.real: The Pony Express ran for only about 18 months, from April 1860 to October 1861, before the telegraph put it out of business.

cards.say: [Julius Caesar was kidnapped by pirates and demanded a bigger ransom], [Peter the Great made Russian men pay a tax to keep their beards], [Alexander the Great was personally tutored as a teenager by Plato], and [Mansa Musa spent so much gold in Cairo that its value crashed].
cards.real: Alexander's teenage tutor was Aristotle, a former student of Plato. Plato had died years earlier, when Alexander was a young boy.

cards.say: [The first chocolate bar was made in Switzerland], [Caesar salad was invented in Tijuana, Mexico], [cotton candy was co-invented by a dentist], and [ketchup was once sold as medicine in pill form].
cards.real: The first solid chocolate bar was made by J.S. Fry and Sons in Bristol, England, in 1847. The Swiss came later, with milk chocolate.

cards.say: [Julia Child worked for a US spy agency before she became a chef], [J.R.R. Tolkien once worked on the Oxford English Dictionary], [Florence Nightingale was the first person ever to draw a pie chart], and [Marie Curie's notebooks are still too radioactive to handle without gear].
cards.real: William Playfair drew the first known pie chart in 1801. Nightingale did make a famous chart of her own, the rose diagram.

cards.say: [The Statue of Liberty worked as an official lighthouse until 1902], [P.T. Barnum marched 21 elephants across the Brooklyn Bridge], [the Empire State Building's spire was built as a dock for airships], and [the Leaning Tower of Pisa began to tilt 200 years after it was finished].
cards.real: The tower started leaning in 1178, during construction, when builders reached the second floor. That's partly why it took almost 200 years to finish.

cards.say: [When the Mona Lisa was stolen in 1911, police questioned Pablo Picasso], [Mozart wrote the tune of Twinkle Twinkle Little Star at age five], [Napoleon wrote a short romance novel years before he became emperor], and [the first Academy Awards ceremony lasted just 15 minutes].
cards.real: The melody is an old French folk song. Mozart wrote a set of variations on it in his twenties, which is why it gets credited to him.

cards.say: [The first speeding ticket was for going 8 miles an hour], [the world's first traffic light exploded less than a month after it went up], [the world's first underground railway opened in New York City], and [the first animals ever sent into space were a batch of fruit flies].
cards.real: The first underground railway was London's Metropolitan Railway, opened in 1863. New York's subway didn't open until 1904.

cards.say: [Three of the first five US presidents died on the Fourth of July], [most signers of the Declaration of Independence signed it in August], [the White House didn't get its official name until 1901], and [Paul Revere made it all the way to Concord on his famous midnight ride].
cards.real: Revere was stopped by a British patrol before he reached Concord. Samuel Prescott, who escaped the same patrol, carried the warning there.

cards.say: [Albert Einstein won his Nobel Prize for the theory of relativity], [the first computer mouse had a body carved out of wood], [Ben Franklin invented swim fins for his hands as a kid], and [a British man who never visited the US paid to found the Smithsonian].
cards.real: Einstein's 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded for his explanation of the photoelectric effect, not for relativity.

cards.say: [The only casualty of the 1859 Pig War between the US and Britain was a pig], [the Pilgrims wore tall black hats with shiny buckles on the front], [Monopoly sets smuggled escape maps to prisoners of war in World War II], and [the US bought Alaska from Russia for about two cents an acre].
cards.real: Buckles weren't in fashion until later in the 1600s. The buckled Pilgrim hat comes from artwork made in the 1800s.
